config.title: Build typed command bus

intro.title: Build typed command bus
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed command bus, a design pattern that helps manage and execute different commands in a type-safe way. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's generic types to ensure each command has a specific structure and returns a predictable result. The main constructs involved are interfaces, generic functions, and type parameters to enforce correctness at compile time. By the end, you'll have a reusable command bus that can handle various operations while preventing common type errors.
intro.usecase: A typed command bus is a foundational pattern in large-scale applications like e-commerce platforms and financial dashboards, where user actions must be processed reliably and consistently. For example, when a user submits an order form, clicks a 'filter' button on a data table, or opens a settings modal, each action can be dispatched as a strongly-typed command. This ensures that the system handles inputs—such as order details, filter criteria, or configuration changes—with validated data structures and clear execution flows, reducing bugs and improving maintainability in complex UIs.

objectives: Implement a generic Command interface to enforce type safety across different commands
Construct a CommandBus class with typed methods for registering and executing commands
Configure command handlers that process specific command types and return typed results
Initialize and instantiate the CommandBus with registered handlers for different command types
Manipulate the command execution flow by adding middleware for cross-cutting concerns
Apply the typed command bus to dispatch commands and handle results in a sample application
Integrate error handling within the command bus to manage execution failures gracefully

steps.title: Define Command interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'Command' with a 'type' property of type 'string' and a 'payload' property of type 'any'.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the two properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript interface that defines the shape for command objects in your command bus.
successCriteria: The Command interface is defined with 'type: string' and 'payload: any' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface has both 'type' and 'payload' properties with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Check that you used 'interface Command' with both properties.

steps.title: Define CommandHandler type
steps.instruction: Create a type alias named CommandHandler that represents a function taking a Command and returning void.
steps.hint: Use the type keyword to define an alias for a function type. The function should accept a parameter of type Command and return void.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: a type alias for a function
type Greeter = (name: string) => void;

steps.expectedOutcome: A type alias CommandHandler is defined, representing a function that takes a Command and returns void.
successCriteria: The CommandHandler type alias is defined with the correct function signature.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure CommandHandler is a type alias for a function that takes a Command and returns void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CommandHandler type alias is not defined correctly. It should be a function type that accepts a Command and returns void.

steps.title: Create CommandBus class
steps.instruction: Create a class named CommandBus with a private handlers property of type Map<string, CommandHandler>.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword to define CommandBus. Inside the class, declare a private property called handlers with the specified type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CommandBus class with a private handlers property typed as Map<string, CommandHandler>.
successCriteria: CommandBus class is defined with a private handlers property of type Map<string, CommandHandler>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that the handlers property is private and has the exact type Map<string, CommandHandler>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CommandBus class or its handlers property is missing or incorrect. Ensure you define the class with a private handlers property of type Map<string, CommandHandler>.

steps.title: Implement register method
steps.instruction: Inside the CommandBus class, add a public method named 'register' that takes two parameters: 'commandType' (string) and 'handler' (CommandHandler), and stores them in the 'handlers' map.
steps.hint: Use the Map's set method to associate the commandType with its handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CommandBus class now has a register method that can store command handlers.
successCriteria: The register method is defined with correct parameters and stores the handler in the handlers map.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the method signature matches (commandType: string, handler: CommandHandler) and uses this.handlers.set().
steps.feedbackWrong: The register method is missing or incorrect. It should accept a command type string and a CommandHandler, then store them in the handlers map.

steps.title: Implement execute method
steps.instruction: Add an execute method to the CommandBus class that takes a Command object, finds the appropriate handler using the command's type, and executes it.
steps.hint: The method should look up the handler in the handlers Map using the command.type as the key, then call the handler with the command.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CommandBus class will have an execute method that can dispatch commands to their registered handlers.
successCriteria: The execute method is added to CommandBus, takes a Command parameter, retrieves the handler using command.type, and calls the handler with the command.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check that it correctly looks up the handler and calls it with the command.
steps.feedbackWrong: The execute method is missing or doesn't properly handle command execution.

steps.title: Add error handling for missing handlers
steps.instruction: In the execute method of the CommandBus class, add a check to throw an error when no handler is found for the command's type.
steps.hint: Before calling the handler, check if the handlers Map has an entry for the command type. If not, throw an Error with a descriptive message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The execute method will now throw an error when trying to execute a command with an unregistered type.
successCriteria: The execute method includes a check for the handler's existence and throws an Error if missing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the error handling isn't complete. Make sure to check if the handler exists before calling it, and throw an Error with a clear message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The execute method doesn't yet handle missing handlers. Add a check to see if the handler exists in the Map before calling it, and throw an Error if it doesn't.

steps.title: Create specific command interfaces
steps.instruction: Create two new interfaces: AddUserCommand and RemoveUserCommand that extend the Command interface. Add specific payload properties to each interface.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword with 'extends Command'. Add a 'payload' property with appropriate types for each command.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two new interfaces that extend Command with specific payload properties are created.
successCriteria: AddUserCommand and RemoveUserCommand interfaces exist, both extend Command, and each has a payload property with appropriate types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure both interfaces extend Command and include appropriate payload properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interfaces should extend Command and include payload properties. Check the syntax for interface extension.

steps.title: Create command bus instance
steps.instruction: Create an instance of the CommandBus class and store it in a variable named 'commandBus'.
steps.hint: Use the 'new' keyword followed by the class name to instantiate the CommandBus.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an instance of a class
const myInstance = new MyClass();
steps.expectedOutcome: A CommandBus instance is created and stored in a variable.
successCriteria: A variable named 'commandBus' is declared and assigned a new CommandBus instance.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating a new CommandBus instance and storing it in a variable named 'commandBus'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CommandBus instance wasn't created correctly. Remember to use the 'new' keyword and store it in a variable named 'commandBus'.

steps.title: Register handlers for specific commands
steps.instruction: In your CommandBus instance, register two handlers: one for the 'add-user' command type and one for the 'remove-user' command type. Use the register method you implemented earlier.
steps.hint: Call the register method on your CommandBus instance twice, passing the command type string and a handler function for each.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your CommandBus instance will have two handlers registered, ready to handle 'add-user' and 'remove-user' commands.
successCriteria: Two calls to commandBus.register exist: one for 'add-user' with a handler function, and one for 'remove-user' with a handler function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've registered at least one handler, but both 'add-user' and 'remove-user' need handlers. Make sure you call register for each command type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handlers aren't registered yet. Use the register method on your commandBus instance to add a handler for 'add-user' and another for 'remove-user'.

steps.title: Execute commands with the bus
steps.instruction: Create an AddUserCommand object and execute it using the commandBus.execute() method.
steps.hint: Instantiate an object with the required properties for the AddUserCommand interface and pass it to commandBus.execute().
steps.expectedOutcome: The command bus will process the AddUserCommand through its execute method, demonstrating the typed command bus in action.
successCriteria: An AddUserCommand object is created with type 'add-user' and a username property, and commandBus.execute() is called with that object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress. Ensure you create a complete AddUserCommand object with both type and username, then call commandBus.execute() with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating an object that matches the AddUserCommand interface, then pass it to commandBus.execute().
